case: Investigation into the alleged theft of a mobile phone at the Ötkert club (21 June 2024)
description: Prosecutors are investigating an incident in the early hours of 21 June 2024 at the Ötkert club in Budapest, in which, according to the Prosecutor General's Office, Magyar took the mobile phone of a man who was filming him and deliberately dropped it into the Danube; in September 2024 the prosecution said this conduct could constitute theft. Because Magyar had become an MEP, the Hungarian authorities asked the European Parliament to waive his immunity. The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) recommended keeping it (18 votes to 7, 23 September 2025) and the plenary rejected the waiver on 7 October 2025. After his EP mandate ended in May 2026 the investigation was resumed, and the Prosecutor General's Office asked the National Assembly to suspend his immunity as an MP. Magyar asked parliament to do so, saying he takes responsibility for his actions and had acted to protect young people he said were being attacked; he has called the case an attempt at political character assassination.
outcome: On 28 September 2026 the National Assembly suspended Magyar's parliamentary immunity in this case by 139 votes to 0 (Fidesz–KDNP MPs did not vote), against the recommendation of its immunity committee. As of October 2026 the case is at the investigation stage; no charge had been reported in the sources consulted.
court: Prosecution Service of Hungary (Legfőbb Ügyészség); European Parliament (immunity, 2024–2025); National Assembly (immunity, 2026)
presumption_note: Investigation only: Magyar has not been charged or tried and is presumed innocent. The European Parliament's 2025 decision concerned only his immunity, not the merits of the case.
key_facts: Incident on 21 June 2024; prosecutors said in September 2024 that taking the phone could amount to theft
European Parliament refused to lift his immunity on 7 October 2025, following a JURI vote of 18 to 7
Investigation resumed after his EP mandate ended; Hungarian parliament lifted his immunity on 28 September 2026 (139–0) at his own request

case: Defamation (becsületsértés) proceedings and related European Parliament immunity requests (2024–2025)
type: private prosecutions for defamation / immunity waiver requests
description: Besides the phone case, the European Parliament received two further requests in November 2024 and May 2025 to waive Magyar's immunity in defamation proceedings over remarks he made about other politicians, which Infostart describes as defamation cases brought by private (substitute private) prosecutors rather than by the state prosecution. According to EUrologus, cited by Telex, one was brought by former Fidesz MP György Simonka. The third request was not officially identified; Mi Hazánk leader László Toroczkai had announced in April 2025 that a defamation complaint had been filed against Magyar over his statements about the party, and that the proceedings had been suspended because of his immunity. The Prosecutor General's Office said it had filed only the phone-case request.
outcome: The European Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee recommended rejecting the requests (23 September 2025) and the plenary upheld Magyar's immunity in all cases on 7 October 2025. The sources consulted do not report that these defamation proceedings resumed after Magyar left the European Parliament and became an MP in May 2026.
court: Hungarian courts (private defamation prosecutions); European Parliament (immunity decisions)
presumption_note: No judgment has been given on the merits; the European Parliament ruled only on immunity. Magyar is presumed innocent of the alleged defamation.
key_facts: Three immunity waiver requests concerning Magyar reached the European Parliament between October 2024 and May 2025
Two concerned defamation proceedings brought by private parties
The European Parliament upheld his immunity in all three cases on 7 October 2025

case: Insider-trading allegations concerning OPUS Global shares bought in 2023
type: market-supervision proceeding (Magyar Nemzeti Bank) and criminal investigation
description: Press reports in early 2025 alleged that on 21 July 2023, shortly before the stock-market close, Magyar sold other shares and bought tens of millions of forints' worth of OPUS Global shares, hours before the company announced a share buyback that raised their price, and sold them after the market opened on 24 July. The Hungarian National Bank (MNB), which had opened a market-supervision procedure in September 2023 against several people over OPUS trading, extended it on 28 November 2024 to the OPUS shares bought by Magyar, and closed the procedure concerning him in November 2025. Prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into suspected insider trading (bennfentes kereskedelem) in early 2025 after a complaint by István Tényi; Fidesz MP Gyula Budai filed a further complaint on 26 November 2025. According to HVG, no suspect had been named a year into the investigation. Magyar denied any wrongdoing throughout.
outcome: The MNB ended its procedure concerning Magyar in November 2025. The Central Chief Prosecutor's Investigation Office (Központi Nyomozó Főügyészség) discontinued the criminal proceedings on 23 March 2026 because, on the available data and evidence, no criminal offence could be established; the decision was made public only after the April 2026 election.
court: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (market supervision); Központi Nyomozó Főügyészség (Central Chief Prosecutor's Investigation Office)
presumption_note: Magyar was never charged or formally named a suspect; both the MNB procedure concerning him and the criminal proceedings were closed without any finding against him.
key_facts: Alleged OPUS Global share purchases on 21 July 2023, before a buyback announcement
MNB extended its market-supervision procedure to Magyar's OPUS purchases on 28 November 2024 and closed it concerning him in November 2025
Criminal investigation opened in early 2025 after a complaint; no suspect named according to HVG (February 2026)
Criminal proceedings discontinued on 23 March 2026: no offence established

case: Witness testimony in the Schadl–Völner bribery investigation (March 2024)
description: Magyar was summoned as a witness by the Budapest Investigating Prosecutor's Office (Fővárosi Nyomozó Ügyészség) in the corruption case involving György Schadl, former head of the court bailiffs' chamber, and Pál Völner, former state secretary for justice. He testified for about four hours on 20 March 2024, accompanied by two lawyers, about statements he had made on Facebook, and was called back for a continued hearing on 26 March 2024, the day he published his recording of Judit Varga discussing the case files.
outcome: Witness only; Magyar is not a suspect or defendant in the Schadl–Völner case.
court: Fővárosi Nyomozó Ügyészség (Budapest Investigating Prosecutor's Office)
presumption_note: Magyar appeared solely as a witness; no allegation of wrongdoing against him is involved in this proceeding.
key_facts: Witness hearing on 20 March 2024, recorded on video and audio

case: Press-correction lawsuits (helyreigazítási perek) against pro-government media over reporting on the Ötkert incident
description: After pro-government outlets reported that Magyar had harassed women at the Ötkert club in June 2024, he brought press-correction suits against several of them. By 9 September 2024 he reported his eighth favourable judgment, against Mandiner, which was ordered to publish that it had falsely spread the claim that he had harassed women at the club and to pay 2,000 euros in costs; HVG reported that he had won every such case against government-aligned media up to then.
outcome: Courts ruled in Magyar's favour in the reported cases and ordered corrections (eight judgments by September 2024, according to Magyar's statement reported by HVG). Later appeals were not tracked in the sources consulted.
presumption_note: Civil proceedings in which Magyar is the plaintiff; they involve no accusation against him.
key_facts: Eight favourable judgments reported by September 2024
Mandiner ordered to publish a correction and pay 2,000 euros in costs
